items.title: What Is Given: Sentient Gifts, and the Beginning of Material Gifts

items.zh: 用何施者，謂若略說，或用有情數物而行惠施，或用無情數物而行惠施。云何有情數物持用惠施？謂或妻子、奴婢、作使，或象、馬猪牛、羊、雞、鴨、駝、騾等類，或有諸餘大男、大女、小男、小女，或復所餘如是等類所用施物。或復內身頭、目、手、足、血、肉、骨、髓隨願施與，此亦名為有情數物持用布施。是諸菩薩所現行事，非此義中意所許施。若有於彼諸有情類，或得自在，或有勢力，或能制伏。若應持彼惠施於他；若惠施時自無有罪；若不由彼惠施因緣，他心嫌恨；若施於他，知彼有情不為損惱；是名無罪有情數物持用惠施。云何無情數物持用惠施？謂略說有三種物。一者、財物，二者、穀物，三者、處物。言財物者，謂末尼、真珠、琉璃、螺貝、璧玉、珊瑚、馬瑙彩石、生色可染、赤珠右旋。復有所餘如是等類，或諸珍寶、或金、或銀、或諸衣服、或諸什物、或香、或鬘。是名財物。云何穀物？謂諸所有可食可飲，大麥、小麥、稻穀、粟穀、糜黍、胡麻、大小豆等，甘蔗、蒲桃、乳酪、果汁、種種漿飲。復有所餘如是等類，是名穀物。
items.en: With what does one give? Briefly, one gives either using sentient possessions, or using non-sentient possessions. … Namely, one's spouse and children, servants, attendants; or elephants, horses, pigs, cattle, sheep, chickens, ducks, camels, or mules; or other men, women, boys, or girls in one's care. … If one has genuine authority, power, or control over such beings … this is called blameless giving of sentient possessions. What is giving of non-sentient possessions? Briefly, there are three kinds: wealth, grain, and dwelling places.

items.title: Grain and Dwellings Close Material Gifts; the Manner of Giving

items.zh: 云何處物？謂諸田宅、邸店、鄽肆，建立福舍及寺館等。復有所餘如是等類，是名處物。是名無罪無情數物持用惠施。當知此中，有情數物、無情數物，一切總說名所用施。何相施者，謂無貪俱行思造作心意業，及此所起身業、語業，捨所施物。或自相續，或他相續。是名施相。
items.en: What are dwelling-places? Fields, houses, inns, shops, charitable halls, temples, and lodges. … Know that sentient and non-sentient possessions together are called what is given. In what manner does one give? It means the mental karma of volition accompanied by non-attachment, together with the bodily and verbal karma that arises from it, in relinquishing the gift — whether through one's own continuity, or through another's. This is called the manner of giving.

items.title: Section: How to Give — Seven Qualities That Make Giving Genuine

items.zh: 云何施者，謂由淨信而行惠施；由正教見而行惠施；由有果見而行惠施；由極殷重而行惠施；由恭敬心自手行施，而不輕慢；應時而施，濟他要用；不損惱他而行惠施。如法平等，不以兇暴積集財物而行惠施，以鮮潔物而行惠施，以精妙物而行惠施，以清淨物而行惠施。由此自他俱無有罪，數數惠施制伏慳垢，積集勢力而行惠施。先心歡喜而行惠施，於正施時其心清淨，施已無悔。如是而施。
items.en: How does one give? By giving with genuine faith; by giving with correct understanding; by giving with an understanding of its results; by giving with the utmost earnestness; by giving respectfully with one's own hand, never with contempt; by giving at the right time, meeting an actual need; by giving without causing distress. … Lawfully and impartially … giving with a genuinely pure object. … Giving again and again overcomes the taint of stinginess … with a joyful mind beforehand, a pure mind during the act itself, and no regret afterwards. This is how one gives.

items.title: Section: Why One Gives, and Generosity Closes in Full

items.zh: 何故施者，或慈悲故而行惠施，謂於有苦。或知恩故而行惠施，謂於有恩。或愛、或敬、或信順故而行惠施，謂於親愛。或為悕求世出世間殊勝功德而行惠施，謂於尊勝。由是因緣，故修惠施。由是行相，或在家者、或出家者修行布施，為莊嚴心、為助伴心、為資瑜伽、為得上義而行布施。由此因緣，施性無罪，是名惠捨。
items.en: Why does one give? Out of compassion, towards those in hardship. Out of gratitude, towards those who have shown kindness. Out of affection, respect, or trust, towards those held dear. Or in pursuit of excellent worldly and world-transcending qualities, towards the venerable. For these reasons, one practices giving. … By means of these characteristics, whether a householder or a renunciant practices giving, it is undertaken to adorn the mind, to support the mind, to provide the resources for yogic practice, and to attain the highest good. For this reason, the nature of such giving is blameless — this is called generosity.

items.title: Section: The Final Provision Opens — The Ornaments of a Genuine Renunciant

items.zh: 云何名為沙門莊嚴？嗢拕南曰：正信、而無諂、少病、精進、慧、具少欲、喜足、易養、及易滿、杜多德、端嚴、知量、善士法、具聰慧者相、忍、柔和、賢善。謂如有一，具足正信、無有諂曲、少諸疾病、性勤精進、成就妙慧、少欲、喜足、易養、易滿、具足成就杜多功德、端嚴、知量、具足成就賢善士法、具足成就聰慧者相、堪忍、柔和、為性賢善。
items.en: What is meant by the ornaments of a renunciant? A summary verse says: full faith and freedom from deceit; few illnesses, diligence, wisdom; few desires and contentment; ease of support and ease of satisfaction; the virtues of ascetic practice, dignified bearing; a sense of proper measure, the qualities of a good person; the marks of a wise person; patience, gentleness, and innate goodness. It is like one who is possessed of full faith, free of deceit, rarely ill, diligent by nature, accomplished in excellent wisdom, of few desires, contented, easy to support, easy to satisfy, fully accomplished in the virtues of ascetic practice, dignified in bearing, possessed of a sense of proper measure, fully accomplished in the qualities of a good person, fully accomplished in the marks of a wise person, patient, gentle, and good-natured by disposition.

items.title: Full Faith: Reverence Extended to Every Dimension of Practice

items.zh: 云何名為具足正信？謂多淨信、多正敬順、多生勝解、多善欲樂。於諸善法及大師所深生淨信，無惑無疑；於大師所恭敬尊重承奉供養；既修如是恭敬尊重承奉供養，專心親附，依止而住。如於大師，如是於法同梵行者、於諸所學教授教誡、於修供養、於無放逸、於三摩地，當知亦爾。如是名為具足正信。
items.en: What is meant by full faith? It means abundant pure faith, abundant genuine reverence and compliance, abundant resolute understanding, and abundant wholesome aspiration. One holds deep, pure faith in wholesome teachings and in the great Teacher, free of doubt or uncertainty; one reveres, honours, serves, and makes offerings to the Teacher; and, having cultivated such reverence, honour, service, and offering, one draws close with a devoted mind and abides in reliance upon him. Just as towards the great Teacher, so too towards fellow practitioners of pure conduct in the Dharma, towards the instruction and guidance one has received, towards the practice of making offerings, towards vigilance, and towards meditative concentration — know that the same applies in each case. This is called full faith.

blocks.text: Generosity in detail, then the last provision: the "ornaments" of a renunciant.

"Sentient possessions or non-sentient possessions." Master Cháng Bǎi: a hearer may give external things; the giving of one's own body belongs to the bodhisattva path. Non-sentient gifts are wealth, grain, and "dwelling places": fields, houses, inns, halls. Venerable Miào Jìng: "real estate". And 寺 in early usage meant a government building, not a temple.

"With genuine faith; with correct understanding; with understanding of its results; with the utmost earnestness; respectfully with one's own hand; at the right time; without harming others." Master Cháng Bǎi: at the right time means "an umbrella while it is raining, a cup of water when someone is thirsty".

"Out of compassion, towards those in hardship; out of gratitude, towards those who have shown kindness; out of affection, respect, or trust, towards those held dear"; or in pursuit of worldly and transcendent good.

A summary verse lists them: full faith, freedom from deceit, few illnesses, diligence, wisdom, few desires, contentment, being easy to support and satisfy, the ascetic virtues, dignity, proper measure, the qualities of a good person, wisdom, patience, gentleness, innate goodness.

"Abundant pure faith, reverence, resolute understanding, and wholesome aspiration", towards the teachings, the Teacher, and fellow practitioners. Venerable Miào Jìng: those studying the same practice.

quiz.q: What three kinds of non-sentient gifts are there, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say "dwelling places" are?
options: wealth, grain, and dwelling places — real estate
quiz.why: "Briefly, there are three kinds: wealth, grain, and dwelling places." Venerable Miào Jìng: "dwelling places" are real estate.

quiz.q: Why, according to Master Cháng Bǎi, does a hearer not yet give away their own body?
options: the hearer still has the path to cultivate, so for now gives only external things
quiz.why: "One gives either using sentient possessions, or using non-sentient possessions." Master Cháng Bǎi: a hearer may give external things, but since they still have the noble path to cultivate, at this stage they do not give away their whole body. The bodhisattva's gift of the body was left out of the edition's text.

quiz.q: The English renders 寺館 as "temples, and lodges." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read it?
options: 寺 is a government office building; 館 is an inn
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 寺 here is a government office building; 館 is an inn and the like. In early usage 寺 meant a government office; the English reads it as a temple.

quiz.q: What examples does Master Cháng Bǎi give for "giving at the right time, meeting an actual need"?
options: an umbrella in rain, water when thirsty, money when short
quiz.why: "By giving at the right time, meeting an actual need." Master Cháng Bǎi: such as giving an umbrella while it is raining, a cup of water when someone is thirsty, money when someone is short.

quiz.q: Why does one give — with what motive towards each of the four recipients?
options: compassion towards the suffering, gratitude towards benefactors, affection and trust towards the dear, and seeking excellent qualities towards the venerable
quiz.why: "Out of compassion, towards those in hardship. Out of gratitude, towards those who have shown kindness …" Venerable Miào Jìng: the motive is compassion — relieving their suffering and giving them ease.

quiz.q: How many ornaments does the summary verse list, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: two verses, seventeen ornaments, then set out in prose
quiz.why: The summary verse: full faith and freedom from deceit; few illnesses, diligence, wisdom; few desires and contentment; ease of support and satisfaction; ascetic virtues, dignified bearing; proper measure, a good person's qualities; the marks of the wise; patience, gentleness, innate goodness. Venerable Miào Jìng: these two verses give seventeen ornaments; the prose follows.

quiz.q: The English splits "法同梵行者" into "towards the Dharma, towards fellow practitioners." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read it?
options: as one term — fellow practitioners of the same Dharma gate
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the term indicates fellow practitioners in one Dharma gate — those studying the same practice.
